> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7b926f76007316ec13d2b17ec4b0a316b94e4d7e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ceb31bd703294af94235a00fab7457cf66e3c0e2` — the merge of head `6e141edcad84a65d7e2128af7fc901b51289fed2` into base `7b926f76007316ec13d2b17ec4b0a316b94e4d7e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ceb31bd703294af94235a00fab7457cf66e3c0e2 && git checkout ceb31bd703294af94235a00fab7457cf66e3c0e2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7b926f76007316ec13d2b17ec4b0a316b94e4d7e 6e141edcad84a65d7e2128af7fc901b51289fed2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7b926f76007316ec13d2b17ec4b0a316b94e4d7e && git merge --no-ff 6e141edcad84a65d7e2128af7fc901b51289fed2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7b926f76007316ec13d2b17ec4b0a316b94e4d7e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7b926f76007316ec13d2b17ec4b0a316b94e4d7e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

It corrects one "still not judged" line in each of four pending changesets that this PR did not add, and the PR adds its own. That is the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class. `pr-automation.yml:937`–`:947` leaves it RED BY DESIGN on a PR that "corrects a note AND adds its own (the foreign-changeset refusal)".
- **Why it may stay red:**

No `skip-changeset` label is applied: this PR adds a real changeset.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6e141edcad84a65d7e2128af7fc901b51289fed2`
Local-runs: none

Read at 2026-10-08T08:06Z by `session_01LAi5BVvQNiYzepSAcsoFLK`, on PR #22233 (pass 4 of #22032), against the merge base `3b493184e1` (an ancestor of the head, which merges it). Inputs: the card's body and its 23 comments, the PR body, its 14-file list and the net diff, the head's check-runs, and the binding text named below, read through `git` against the fetched refs and `gh api`. Nothing was built, run or re-run. The seat's ACCEPT `6055367205` was read as a map, not as evidence.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The lift is exactly one guard.** A comment-stripped diff of `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` between the base and the head is one line: the object action loop's `for (const obj of objectWrite ? [] : objects)` becomes `for (const obj of objects)`. The four other `objectWrite` guards read unchanged — flows (base `:1557`, head `:1569`), the top-level `actions` (`:2248` to `:2263`), `sharingRules` (`:2265` to `:2286`) and `hooks` (`:2280` to `:2301`) — and `checkAction` is byte-identical at both commits. `authoring-rules.ts` moves comments and docblocks only: the registry entry keeps `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'action', 'hook', 'object']` and `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, so `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('object')` still lists `validateStackExpressions`, and the one doc line on `AuthoringRuleContext.runtimeWriteType` reaches the built declarations. `runtime-gate.ts`, `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` and `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` are untouched. Rider 1 is one word in a comment (`'admin'` to `'org_admin'`).

**(b) The door's verdict is the build's.** Both doors reach the same call: the entry's `run` maps `runStackExpressionPasses(stack, { runtimeWriteType: ctx.runtimeWriteType })` to findings in one place (`severity`, `rule: EXPRESSION_INVALID`, `where`, `path` equal to `where`, `message`, `hint`); the build passes no `runtimeWriteType`, the gate passes the write's type (`runtime-gate.ts:1102`). `checkAction` is the one judge of `visible` (always) and `disabled` (unless a boolean literal), through the same `check(…, obj, 'record')`, so on an object-only body the door's finding is the build's finding by construction. Pinned at both doors: the lint PARITY test (`toEqual` over 6 refused bodies) and the protocol (d) test (key by key on `rule`, `where`, `path`, `message` and `hint`, severity asserted `error`). The one divergence is a location, pinned and true of the source: an action also declared top-level is claimed by the build's stack loop first (`seenActions`, keyed on object and name) and located at `stack · action`, while an object write carries no top-level `actions` and locates it at the object. The build refuses that predicate too, so it is not a door-only refusal and leaves the narrowing claim intact.

**(c) `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds.** The only source change removes a guard, so the door's finding set on an object write is a superset of the former and, by the enumeration pin's own assertion, exactly the build's findings on the object's body (`onObjectWrite` equals `all.filter(LIFTED_SITES)`). Nothing is newly accepted: no check is removed, the validator's vocabulary is not widened, there is no exemption, and `sys-approval-request.object.ts` is untouched. Nothing the build accepts is newly refused: 8 CONTROL shapes (lint) and 4 shipped shapes (protocol) are asserted clean at both doors, and the reports' corpus readings (118 objects from `*.object.ts` and 33 composed, 117 predicates) refuse exactly the 8 `sys_approval_request` sites the build already refuses, at both shapes, and 0 in the examples. The lift's one measured effect outside the hatch is the refusal code on one packaged object's publish save (the per-kernel table, (e)), ruled F1 in `6054240056`.

**(d) The pins.** Lint door (`runtime-gate.object-action-predicate-writes.test.ts`, 19 tests): 6 LIT refusals — `visible` for a bare reference, an unregistered function, an unknown field and a syntax error; `disabled` for a bare reference and a syntax error — each located at `object 'fx_action' · action 'fx_close' KEY` and matched on the finding's named subject; 8 CONTROL shapes accepted and asserted clean at the build too; PARITY; LOCATION; a refused stored sibling not blocking a clean save; a broken stored self (a clean save passes, re-saving the broken body is refused). Protocol door (`protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`, 11 tests through the real `saveMetaItem`, `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts`): three refusals asserted on `{ code: 'INVALID_METADATA', status: 422 }` with `rulesRun`, path, where, severity and subject, and no row landed; the card's shape refused on a draft's promotion and on a package draft publish (`outcome: 'refused'`, the row left `draft`); four shipped shapes landing `active`; the sibling case; parity. The enumeration pin (`runtime-gate.object-formula-writes.test.ts`) is not weakened: the old pin held one `FENCED_SITES` entry beside three `LIFTED_SITES`, asserted the build with `includes` and the door with `toEqual`; the new pin holds five `LIFTED_SITES` (the action's `visible` and `disabled` join), asserts the build with an exact `toEqual`, the door with `toEqual`, and adds a second half the old pin never had — a top-level action, a flow edge, a sharing rule and a hook bound to the same object, with the build's nine-site walk order asserted, a flow write still equal to the build, and an object write exactly the five object-borne sites. The dropped `|| i.where === WHERE` term was dead (the formula is clean, and the first test asserts it is not flagged). A fence re-added on any object-borne pass, or a pass over another collection reaching the door, turns it red.

**(e) The per-kernel table is true of the source.** `saveMetaItem` at the head: `refusePackagedBaseOverride` at `protocol.ts:20257`, inside `if (this.environmentId !== undefined)` (`:20248`); the authoring gate `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` at `:20735`, with `state: mode === 'draft' ? 'draft' : 'active'`, and the gate returns `[]` on a non-`active` state; `repo.put` at `:21048`, and `put` calls `assertAllowed(ref, 'save', …)` at `sys-metadata-repository.ts:730`, the emitter of `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. So on a host-config kernel a publish save meets the gate (422 after the lift) before the repository's package door (403), and a draft save skips the gate and meets that door (403) — row 1. Under the hatch, `isOverlayAllowed` folds `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` in, so the package door admits the write and the gate alone answers: publish 200 before and 422 after, draft 200 — row 2. On an environment-scoped kernel the package door answers 403 above the gate, in both modes — row 3. The drift sentence states exactly that order and hands it to #22220; it over-claims nothing. One reading the table does not spell out and does not contradict: row 3 names the kernel without a setting, and with the hatch open on an environment kernel the same fold bypasses the package door, so row 2's reading applies there too. #22211 (the producer) and #22220 (the order) are named; both exist, are open, and their titles match the changeset's sentences. The PR body's line references (`:20735`, `:21048`, `:20257`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts:730`) are the head's.

**(f) Rider 2.** Word-diffed: `22019-object-save-door-formula-verdict.md` one line; `22032-object-save-door-validation-predicates.md` one line; `22032-object-save-door-field-rule-slots.md` one line; `22032-object-save-door-option-visible-when.md` one line plus the deleted supersede sentence (+1/−1, +1/−1, +1/−1, +2/−2). Nothing else in those files moved. Compiled with the pass-4 entry, the five say true and consistent things: each entry names the crossing it covers and points the rest at "their own #22032 entries", and all four other crossings are #22032's; `conditionalRequired` is dropped from the rewritten slot lists, consistent with pass 2's untouched line that it is refused at the schema step (true at the head: `field.zod.ts:1838`, `retiredKey`); the pass-4 entry's Unchanged names the top-level `actions`, flows, sharing rules and hooks as not judged on an object write, which is what the four guards do. The present tense "are judged at this door" is true at the compile point the five are written for — pending together; the window before this lands is the one the rulings name, and a release that consumed the four first would surface as a modify/delete conflict on this PR, not silently.

**The gate verdicts, as read.** At the last read of the head's 33 check-runs (the head unmoved, the PR still draft): 28 success, 3 skipped (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, the opt-in tarball smoke), 1 in progress (`Test Core (1/6)`), 1 failure. Of the seven required contexts, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green, and `Test Core` waits on its last lane. The one red is `Check Changeset`, at the step "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR": that step is rule 2 of `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`, the foreign-changeset rule, which refuses a modification of a changeset the PR did not add; `pr-automation.yml` `:937`–`:947` names it RED BY DESIGN on the deliberate-correction class ("corrects a note AND adds its own"), and the ADR-0087 disposition step and the major guard ran past it under `!cancelled()` and passed. `Check Changeset` is not one of the seven required contexts, and its workflow does not run on `merge_group`. The seat's PR comment `6055375818` records the confirmation the gate asks for. Nothing else is red. The in-progress runs are not a FAIL; the seat reads their conclusions before arming.

Not governed: no path under `docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`; 703 changed lines; head repo equals base repo; `Part of #22032` on line 1 and the card stays open.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, with `fix(lint)!`, the ruling's `Clause-②` line, a BREAKING section (the 200-to-422 move on the publish save, the draft promotion and the package publish; the remedy; the per-kernel table naming #22211 and #22220) and the HTML-comment marker `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — the same packages, level and disposition as the three landed object-door entries at the base, read side by side. Checked against the diff: no export, signature, authorable key or stored shape moves (the source change is one guard; the built declarations differ in one doc comment), so nothing calls for a major and nothing is `yes`; the accept set narrows at a door, which AGENTS.md makes BREAKING for `(narrowing)`; the `Guard against accidental major bumps` step and the `Require an ADR-0087 disposition` step are green on this head; no `skip-changeset` label. `metadata-protocol` bumps with no code change of its own, as passes 1–3 did: its `saveMetaItem` verdict moves through its `@objectstack/lint` dependency, and its test file pins it. The disposition holds on the gate's own reading: the Remedy edits a predicate the author wrote, which no ledger entry can derive, so the body carries no migration prescription; the packages publish; no ADR-0087 id covers this door.

The PR's recorded base is `7b926f7600`; this review's net diff is against the merge base `3b493184e1`, which the head contains. The queue rebuilds on current `main`.

They are history read in order, not a live claim, and the claim admitted `authoring-rules.ts` only for a comment naming the fence, which the dev honoured for the current-state sentences.
